title: Handoff sketches and incident synthesis — 2027-03-29
body:
Purpose: quick handoff + synthesis notes for the week of 2027-03-22 → 2027-03-29. Designed to be read during the late-afternoon handoff and used as a checklist for next-shift triage.

Top-line summary:
- Overall external error budget burn: 0.4% (within SLO window, but two short spikes flagged).
- Two customer-impact incidents (partial degradation) — both tied to autoscale race condition + degraded cache hit-rate.
- No data-loss, no expired certs, no auth regressions.

Incidents (short entries):
1) Incident SRE-2071 — "autoscale-race-brief-fanout" — 2027-03-24 02:14UTC → 02:47UTC
   - Symptom: tail latency spike across a subset of dedicated pools when burst traffic arrived.
   - Root cause (current hypothesis): simultaneous scale-up decisions from multiple controllers produced overlapping allocation attempts; transient scheduling thrash and partial node eviction.
   - Mitigation performed: temporary rate-limit on incoming bursts for affected customer routes; triggered fallback to a compatible smaller model variant for 6 minutes.
   - Post-incident note: scheduling logs show a 30–45s window where allocator retried; need more observability on allocator backoff.
   - Owner: Marcus Li (triage) / follow-up: infra-autoscale team.

2) Incident SRE-2090 — "kv-cache-drift-and-hitloss" — 2027-03-26 19:02UTC → 2027-03-26 20:10UTC
   - Symptom: sudden drop in prefix cache hit-rate for hosted-api chat workloads; downstream token cost increased and latency rose 120ms median.
   - Root cause: a config change rolled out to a small fraction of pods disabled an LRU eviction optimization (rollback flag flipped in release-engineering job).
   - Mitigation performed: rollback of the change, manual priming of cache for 10 min, gradual traffic shift.
   - Action: add a canary gate that measures cache-hit delta on deploys that touch caching flags.
   - Owner: Rina Gómez (cache team) / follow-up: add telemetry and alert.

Observations & patterns this week:
- Autoscale race appears correlated to sudden multi-tenant bursts (plausible when onboarding new PLG customers during marketing spikes). Pattern: many small, synchronous scale requests rather than a single large one.
- Cache regressions are frequently introduced by quick config flips; current rollout policy doesn't compare short-window cache metrics pre/post.
- Oncall friction: late-night handoffs often lack clear temporary mitigations in notes — we need a short template.

SLO snapshot (last 7 days):
- request_success (90d-target 99.9%): rolling 7d = 99.62% (error budget remaining but watch for trend).
- p95-latency (target <300ms for hosted default): rolling 7d p95 = 287ms (within target) but p99 had 2 brief spikes to 520ms during SRE-2071.
- cache_hit_ratio (internal objective): weekly average 78% (baseline target 85% for chat profiles).

Handoff checklist (short template to paste into shift notes):
- Current pagers / open incidents: list ticket, short symptom line, who is on it.
- Temporary mitigations applied (yes/no) + how to revert.
- SLOs to watch (top 3): request_success, p99-latency, cache_hit_ratio.
- Key dashboards: "ops/allocator-health", "cache/kv-hitrate-by-pool", "routes/error-burn".
- Suggested next steps (one-line each).

Proposed runbook edits (quick sketches):
1) Autoscaler — add backoff and leader-election window: if >3 concurrent scale intents in 60s for same pool, switch to queued-single-intent and emit "autoscale.throttled" metric.
2) Cache flag rollout — before flag flip: sample 5% traffic path A/B for 10 minutes and compute cache-hit-delta; abort if delta < -5% absolute.
3) Canary rollback detection — deploy job should record metric diffs in the deploy event; alert if p99 latency increases >20% within 10m.

Action items (owners + dates):
- Marcus Li: add allocator backoff metric + small dashboard (due 2027-04-05).
- Rina Gómez: implement canary gate for cache flags in rollout pipeline (draft PR by 2027-04-07).
- Oliver Chan: create a one-paragraph oncall handoff template and add to the oncall-doc page (due 2027-04-01).
- Aisha Patel: triage SRE-2071 logs and extract timeline for postmortem (postmortem draft by 2027-04-06).

Open questions (for product/infra):
- Can product provide expected burst profiles when running PLG campaigns so infra can pre-provision more gracefully? (Ask via #product-ops)
- Is there appetite to reduce flag churn on cache configs—can FE/BE owners batch related changes?

Notes for the next handoff reader:
- If you wake to a p99 spike and allocator shows concurrent intents >2, roll traffic to reserved tier for the affected customer and notify infra-autoscale on-call.
- Prefilled commands:
  - view allocator intents: kubectl -n infra get jobs allocator-intents --selector=pool=POOLNAME --tail=200
  - force small-model-fallback for route: rwctl routes set-fallback --route ROUTE --variant small-quant

Appendix (raw snippets):
- Allocator log excerpt (times truncated): "2027-03-24T02:14:05Z intent create pool=ded-prod-9 id=abcd123" 
  "2027-03-24T02:14:29Z intent create pool=ded-prod-9 id=efgh456" 
  "2027-03-24T02:15:02Z alloc error scheduling node busy"
- Cache telemetry snapshot (2027-03-26 18:50UTC): pool=hosted-chat-a hit=63% → 42% post-deploy; token-cost +24% for that pool.

Quick retrospective note:
- Communication tightness during SRE-2090 was good — the cache team responded and rolled back within 8 minutes of the alert. That should be called out in the postmortem as a win.
- Engineering tradeoff: more conservative rollout gating adds deploy friction but reduces operational noise; propose a short review with product owners.

If anything in here is unclear ping me (Aisha) in #sre-ops or leave a comment on this doc.

-- end --
